content: Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany criticizes UEFA’s Financial Fair Play (FFP) regulations, arguing that they protect established elite clubs rather than preventing financial ruin. Kompany believes these rules hinder new challengers and maintain the dominance of traditional powerhouses like Manchester City. He cites City’s success under Sheikh Mansour’s ownership, attributing their achievements to significant investments that have benefited the local community and contributed to the economy, and argues that such transformations would not be possible under strict FFP guidelines.

Jeff Williams, a 26-year-old England Sevens international who has scored 36 tries on the World Series circuit, has signed with Bath for the upcoming season. Bath head coach Mike Ford and England Sevens head coach Simon Amor both praised Williams' dynamic playing style and his potential to fit well with Bath's attacking approach. Williams, who previously played in South Africa and France, brings valuable experience and talent to the Aviva Premiership side.

In a preview of the upcoming film "Suicide Squad," director David Ayer revealed the first full look at Jared Leto portraying the iconic comic book character, the Joker. Leto has significantly altered his appearance for the role, cutting his hair and shaving his face. The movie, which features the Joker alongside other anti-heroes and villains, is set to hit theaters on August 5, 2016.

Three Florida corrections officers and a former officer trainee were charged with plotting to murder a former inmate as retribution for an earlier altercation, according to the Florida Attorney General's office. The plot came to light when an FBI informant, who had infiltrated a KKK branch, reported the plan to authorities, leading to the staging of a fake crime scene to convince the suspects their victim had been killed. The men now face up to 30 years in prison if found guilty of conspiracy to commit murder.

Manny Pacquiao's conference call about his upcoming fight with Floyd Mayweather was unexpectedly cancelled due to technical difficulties, with over 100 people trying to join the call simultaneously. Pacquiao managed to answer only one question before the call was abruptly ended, to which he responded that his training camp was going very well. The call was rescheduled as an apology was made for the technical issues, and Mayweather was set to have his own call the following day.

Serena Williams celebrated her 700th career victory at the Miami Open with a giant cake, following her victory over Sabine Lisicki in the tournament. Meanwhile, Andy Murray also received a celebratory cake marking his 500th career win. Despite her success, Williams faced a challenge when her sister Venus was defeated in the earlier round, but Serena progressed to the semi-finals where she will face Romania's Simona Halep.

Beijing International Airport is constructing Terminal 1, set to become the world's largest terminal, to accommodate the significant rise in Chinese tourists traveling internationally. Designed by Zaha Hadid and aiming to enhance passenger experience, the terminal will feature a six-tier structure and a spacious layout without pillars, facilitating efficient movement and connectivity. This expansion reflects China's growing influence as a global tourist destination, with Chinese outbound tourism increasing from 10 million in 2000 to 109 million in 2014, contributing $164 billion to the economy.

Manchester United's Wayne Rooney suffered a knee injury during their loss to Everton, as confirmed by manager Louis van Gaal, though the extent of the injury remains unknown. The defeat marked United's first back-to-back league losses under Van Gaal, with Everton climbing into the top half of the table. Van Gaal expressed concern that the setback may allow Liverpool to close in on United’s position in the Champions League qualification race.

Manchester City is reportedly interested in signing Jack Wilshere, who recently shared a photo of his extensive shopping trip on Instagram. The Arsenal midfielder, who has been recovering from ankle surgery, filled his trolley with items like cereal, eggs, and baked beans to aid his recovery. Wilshere humorously captioned his post, asking for help from his followers to unload his shopping trolley.

A Venezuelan woman named Marleni Olivo threw a mango inscribed with her contact information at President Nicolas Maduro during a rally, an act that gained viral attention. In response, Maduro offered Olivo an apartment as part of the country's housing program, fulfilling her request. The incident, while humorous, highlights the polarized political climate in Venezuela, with critics labeling it a "manguicidio" (play on words combining 'mango' and 'magnicidio', meaning assassination).

Carlos Tevez, a former striker for Manchester United and City, believes scoring goals is more challenging in Serie A compared to the Premier League, despite his successful goal-scoring record in Italy. He criticizes the Premier League midfield as "non-existent" and notes that defending in Serie A is tougher due to more crowded defenses. Tevez also expresses confidence in his current team, Juventus, suggesting they have a well-rounded squad capable of achieving great success, including potentially winning the Champions League.

Jamie Carragher criticized Yaya Toure for ducking out of the way of Jason Puncheon's free-kick during Manchester City's loss to Crystal Palace, which effectively ended City's hopes of salvaging a positive result. Carragher argued that Toure should have taken his place in the wall to block the shot, instead of appearing to shy away from the ball. The criticism came as Carragher and Gary Neville discussed the match on Sky Sports' Monday Night Football, with Carragher highlighting how the other players in the wall were clearly preparing to challenge the free-kick.

A 50-year-old Australian man died in Kuta, Bali, after collapsing at a hotel restaurant where he was staying during his holiday. Local reports indicate he likely suffered a heart attack, though an autopsy has yet to be performed to confirm the cause of death. The man was from Seymour, Victoria, and had checked into the hotel on April 19, planning to stay until April 29.

Former Australian cricket captain and commentator Richie Benaud, who passed away at 84 due to skin cancer, was honored with a small, private funeral in Sydney, attended by family and close friends. Despite an offer from the Australian Prime Minister for a state funeral, Benaud’s widow declined, respecting his wish for a quiet send-off. The event, marked by tributes and speeches, underscored Benaud’s significant impact on cricket both as a player and commentator, with memorials continuing in his honor across Australia.

A 16-year-old schoolgirl named Isobel Attwood has been missing from her home in Winchester, Hampshire for two days. She is believed to be with a man in his 20s in Southampton, according to friends who posted on social media. Concerned authorities are appealing for help to locate the teenager, describing her as white, 5ft 4ins tall, and of a small build with brown hair and extensions.

If Manchester City do not qualify for the Champions League this season, key players like Sergio Aguero, David Silva, Joe Hart, and Yaya Toure stand to lose out on significant bonus payments totaling around £12 million for the squad. Manchester City currently sit in fourth place in the Premier League, just four points ahead of Liverpool, with both teams fighting for the final Champions League spot. Despite starting the year well, City have struggled recently, losing seven matches and failing to capitalize on their early successes, which has led their manager to admit the team has "thrown it into the garbage" in recent months.

Martin Skrtel, a Liverpool defender, has denied rumors linking him to potential moves to Wolfsburg or Napoli, stating that his future remains with the Premier League club despite his contract expiring in 2016. His agent has confirmed that Skrtel is set to finalize a new contract with Liverpool, and there are no offers from Wolfsburg as previously reported. Skrtel has recently played in Liverpool's FA Cup semi-final loss to Aston Villa, and the team is expected to undergo significant changes in the summer as they aim to improve their performance and compete for silverware.

Cheryl Rios, a female CEO from Texas, sparked controversy by stating on Facebook that women should not be president due to their "hormones" making them unsuitable for starting wars. Her comments drew widespread criticism and accusations of misogyny. In response, Rios defended her right to hold and express such opinions, emphasizing her belief in equal rights for women in other professions.

Mario Mandzukic, despite suffering injuries in a physical Champions League match against Real Madrid, is expected to be fit for the return leg at the Bernabeu, according to Atletico Madrid's coach Diego Simeone. Simeone believes Mandzukic will be ready to play alongside Antoine Griezmann, who is in good form after adapting to his new attacking position. The second leg is set to take place on Wednesday, following a 0-0 draw in the first leg.

Chelsea's Jose Mourinho had prepared his team to face Marouane Fellaini of Manchester United, only to learn from a hotel doorman that Fellaini wasn't playing due to being there to obtain tickets from Eden Hazard. The Chelsea manager later discovered that it was actually Fellaini's twin brother, Mansour, who had posed for photos at the hotel. Despite the initial confusion, Fellaini did play in the match at Stamford Bridge, which Chelsea won 1-0, putting them within two wins of the Premier League title.

Dawn Milosky, a 45-year-old woman from Beachwood, New Jersey, was involved in a severe accident where her car overturned and caught fire shortly after she was rescued. Police responding to a tip about erratic driving found Milosky unconscious in her overturned 2006 Toyota Solara convertible, which was already emitting smoke and would later ignite. After a quick response, the officers freed Milosky and administered emergency care; she was then airlifted to a hospital and is currently recovering.

A farmer in eastern China has become famous after his goat gave birth to a six-legged kid, nicknamed the "spider goat" by Chinese internet users. The baby goat, born 20 days ago, initially had six legs of similar length but as it grew, two of its front legs became shorter and cannot touch the ground. The farmer, Xiao Qibin, plans to let the unusual goat grow up naturally without attempting to remove the extra legs.

West Ham United are considering signing Javier Hernandez, the Mexican striker who recently scored a crucial Champions League goal for Real Madrid against Atletico Madrid. Hernandez is expected to be available for around £7 million after he returns to Manchester United at the end of his loan deal with Real Madrid. As part of their summer recruitment program, West Ham also aim to sign young players such as Pedro Obiang, Moussa Konate, and Fabian Schar.

Stuart McCall, the manager of Rangers, has dismissed any thoughts of his future with the club being decided before the end of the season, emphasizing that despite recent victories and improved morale, his team has yet to achieve anything significant in the Championship. McCall is confident in his contract extending until the end of the season and beyond, and is focused solely on winning matches, particularly in their upcoming game against Queen of the South. Additionally, Shane Ferguson, a player from Newcastle United, is expected to join Rangers next week, though McCall is cautious about Ferguson's immediate impact due to a recent knee injury.

Werder Bremen secured a 1-0 victory against Hamburg SV through a late penalty kick by Franco Di Santo, securing their position in the race for a Europa League spot. This win, coupled with Hamburg's loss, kept Werder in seventh place with 38 points, while Hamburg dropped to the last position with 25 points. New Hamburg coach Bruno Labbadia, making his debut under adverse circumstances, now faces the challenge of averting the club's first-ever relegation from the Bundesliga.

A two-year-old boy fell into a cheetah exhibit at the Cleveland Metroparks Zoo after slipping between a 10 to 12-foot gap while being held by his parents, who then rescued him. The child was taken to the hospital with minor injuries and was listed in stable condition. The zoo plans to press child endangerment charges against the family involved.

A Russian TV channel, TV Rain, gave Hillary Clinton's 2016 presidential campaign video an 18+ rating due to concerns about the video featuring a gay couple holding hands, potentially violating Russia's anti-gay propaganda law. The channel feared breaking the law, which bans the promotion of non-traditional sexual relationships around minors, and thus marked the video to avoid legal repercussions. This decision came amid Russia's controversial stance on LGBTQ rights, which has faced international criticism and led to various forms of protest both domestically and internationally.

Siem de Jong, Newcastle United's 26-year-old midfielder who returned from a collapsed lung, played 45 minutes for the Under 21s in a reserve match against Derby County, showing a subdued performance. De Jong, who has only made one Premier League start since joining from Ajax, is now hopeful of featuring in the final six matches of the season, though it remains uncertain if he will be fit enough for their upcoming match against Tottenham. Additionally, Facundo Ferreyra, another loan signing who has struggled with injuries, also came on as a substitute at halftime during the match.

Chef Ally Lees of Alfie Bird's restaurant in Birmingham created a massive omelette for Easter that measures three feet in circumference and contains 12,000 calories, equivalent to 16 times the recommended daily protein intake for a man. The omelette, made with 150 eggs, required a specially large paella pan and took an hour to cook thoroughly. Ally advises at least five people to attempt eating this enormous omelette, though he admits he couldn't finish it himself due to its excessive protein content.

Three Olympic gold medalists from London 2012, including Jessica Ennis-Hill, Mo Farah, and Greg Rutherford, will participate in the Sainsbury’s Anniversary Games at the Olympic Stadium. The event features a three-day competition from July 24-26, including a world's only two-day Diamond League meeting, and is expected to recreate the excitement of the 2013 games. Ticket sales have begun, with prices ranging from £10 to £20.

In a shocking discovery, police in Rio de Janeiro uncovered a snack bar that was using the meat of stray dogs to make pastries, including the traditional Brazilian dish pastel. The owner, Chinese Van Ruilonc, admitted to using the meat from the killed dogs, claiming the animals were strays. This finding came alongside the investigation of alleged forced labor conditions for Chinese workers at the establishment.

Ebony Dickens, under the pseudonym Tiffany Milan, posted a controversial and threatening message on Facebook calling for black people to shoot white cops, which led to her arrest by local and federal law enforcement agencies. The post detailed plans to kill multiple police officers, prompting serious concern due to its violent content. Authorities found a firearm and several computers at her home during a subsequent search.

PSV Eindhoven secured their first Dutch championship in seven seasons by defeating Heerenveen 4-1, moving to 79 points and leaving second-place Ajax behind. Key goals came from Luuk de Jong's hat-trick and Memphis Depay's stunning free-kick, while the bottom team Dordrecht suffered another defeat, increasing their relegation worries. Additionally, AZ Alkmaar maintained their position for Europa League playoffs with a 3-1 win over ADO Den Haag.

An 11-year-old boy named Shiva was reportedly beaten to death by his head teacher, Lalit Verma, at Dwarika Prasad School in Railamau village, India, after being accused of stealing a pencil and eraser. The severe beating led to Shiva's death upon arrival at the hospital, with the cause likely being internal bleeding. This incident, which follows other reports of extreme corporal punishment by teachers in India, highlights the serious issues surrounding physical abuse in schools.

A gastrointestinal illness affecting 100 passengers and five crew members has broken out on the Celebrity Infinity cruise ship, which is carrying 2,117 passengers and a crew of 964. The Centers for Disease Control is investigating the cause of the illness, with two agency staff set to board the ship in San Diego on Monday. This is the third such outbreak on the Celebrity Infinity, with previous incidents occurring in 2006 and 2013.

A Boston Terrier named Gizmo, owned by Loren Mathieson, was seen performing an unusual walking technique after trying on new booties, which involved lifting his hind legs in a vertical stance. The amusing footage of Gizmo's "paw-stand walking" has garnered over 80,000 views online. Gizmo appeared unsure about how to walk in his new boots, leading to this comical display of balance and movement.

New Orleans has implemented a city-wide ban on smoking in most public places such as bars, casinos, and restaurants, which took effect at midnight. This decision was made to protect workers like waiters and musicians from secondhand smoke, despite initial concerns from bar owners about potential revenue loss and objections from some smokers. While a legal challenge to the ban is pending, it does not affect many popular tourist activities recommended by CNN.

Manchester United secured a crucial victory over West Ham United in the Under 21 Premier League, moving four points clear at the top of the table. Despite taking an early lead through Josh Cullen's header, West Ham fell behind as Josh Harrop scored twice, with Joe Rothwell adding a third goal. The win came after West Ham had equalized just before halftime through Jordan Brown, but Manchester United capitalized on their opportunity with Harrop's second goal.

The Anglican Archbishop of Brisbane, Phillip Aspinall, has joined a local Catholic priest in advocating for the removal of Queensland's 'gay panic' homicide defense from the state's common law. This legal defense can reduce a murder charge to manslaughter if the defendant claims they felt threatened by a sexual advance. Aspinall emphasized that violence is never a justifiable response to such advances and called for an end to such violent reactions, including those seen in recent anti-Islam rallies and church vandalism incidents.

Sandra Bullock has been named the world's most beautiful woman by People magazine for 2015, marking her as the oldest recipient of the honor in its history. In an interview, Bullock downplays the accolade, emphasizing character and kindness over physical appearance and expressing satisfaction with her life and appearance as a mother and actress. The cover story also highlights Bullock's family life and her efforts to maintain health and fitness beyond her forties.

An improvised bomb explosion near a U.N. vehicle in Garowe, Somalia, killed six people, including four UNICEF aid workers, on Monday morning, prompting Somalia's President to call it an attack against the country's future. Al-Shabaab, the al Qaeda-affiliated terrorist group, claimed responsibility for the attack. This incident follows a separate ambush that resulted in the deaths of three African Union troops in the Lower Shabelle region on Sunday.

Gary Saurage, the manager of Gator Country wildlife park in Beaumont, Texas, was called to capture a large 11-foot, 400-pound alligator from a family's backyard pond using only his hands. The alligator, which had been spotted by Art Williams and his wife near their pond where they keep their grandchildren safe, proved to be particularly aggressive during the capture. After being safely removed, the alligator was taken to Saurage’s park.

In recent clashes between the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) militants and Turkish forces in Agri, eastern Turkey, five PKK militants were killed, one was injured, and four Turkish soldiers were wounded. Turkish Prime Minister Ahmet Davutoglu and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan condemned the attack, while Abdullah Ocalan, the jailed leader of PKK, had previously called for an end to violence and urged his followers to disarm. This conflict, which has lasted over three decades, has claimed an estimated 40,000 lives and involves a struggle for Kurdish independence or a guerrilla war with terrorist acts.

Two 18-month-old twin boys tragically died after accidentally falling into a canal in Yuma, Arizona. The incident occurred around 9:45 AM on Friday, and after a search lasting over an hour, the boys were found in the water. Despite immediate medical attention, the children were pronounced dead upon arrival at the hospital.

Orlando City, a Major League Soccer team coached by Adrian Heath, has shown interest in signing Javier Hernández, the Mexican international who recently had a difficult loan spell at Real Madrid. Despite eight European clubs expressing interest, Hernández could potentially join Orlando City, which has a significant Latin-American fanbase, or remain with Manchester United, who are willing to sell him for around £8 million. Additionally, there is ongoing interest in young Manchester United player Andreas Pereira, with several European clubs, including Paris Saint-Germain and Juventus, showing interest in the 19-year-old midfielder if he does not agree to a new contract with United.

Joel Burger, who shares his last name with the fast-food chain, proposed to his girlfriend Ashley King, and they plan to have a Burger King-themed wedding. The couple, who have known each other since kindergarten, decided to serve drinks in personalized Burger King cups for their guests, despite the possibility of facing some logistical challenges from the company. They began dating just before college and have embraced their unique nickname, "Burger King," which was given to them by a motivational speaker in fifth grade.

A secret police intelligence report from 1964 revealed that a hit band from the 1960s, along with disgraced BBC presenter Jimmy Savile, frequented a notorious pedophile brothel in Battersea, South West London. This information was discovered as part of an investigation into the flat, which was known to be used by pedophiles. Despite the connection between the band and Savile, a detective leading the inquiry noted that this alone did not provide sufficient grounds for further investigation at the time.

Sadie, a German Shepherd from Alberta, Canada, has been caught on camera using her nose to turn on an electric organ and play piano tunes, showcasing her musical abilities. Despite her initial confident performance, Sadie shows signs of musical frustration and even puts a paw to her head, before concluding her impromptu concert with a playful bow. The video of Sadie playing the piano has garnered over 12,000 views and numerous positive comments praising both her performance and intelligence.

A smartphone thief named Ivan Balashov took a selfie in a Russian shop while browsing phones but was caught when police recognized him from the photo. After selecting a preferred phone, he tried to steal it but was stopped by shop security, who allowed him to leave with the phone before he fled. Police used his selfie taken in the shop to identify and arrest him, leading to his conviction and a three-month suspended sentence.

A documentary trailer for the life and music of British singer Amy Winehouse has been released, set for UK release on July 3rd. The film, titled "Amy: The Girl Behind the Name," aims to capture both Winehouse's musical talent and her personal struggles, including her battle with addiction. The documentary will feature extensive unseen footage and previously unheard tracks and has been endorsed by Winehouse's family, who hope it will serve as a tribute to her musical legacy.

The article highlights several TV shows recommended for viewers this week, starting with the return of Christine Baranski and Laurie Metcalf as the mothers of Sheldon and Leonard on "The Big Bang Theory." It also mentions that "Saturday Night Live" will feature Scarlett Johansson as the host, while "Mom" delivers another strong performance from Allison Janney, culminating in the season finale. Additionally, the piece covers the final episodes of "Backstrom," "Blue Bloods," and introduces "Younger," which has been renewed for a second season and is suggested for viewers to catch up on.

Dame Maggie Smith's character, Violet, Countess of Grantham, may return in a new American show called "The Gilded Age," which is set in 19th-century New York and focuses on the wealthy elite. Additionally, Robert and Cora, Earl and Countess of Grantham, might also appear in the series as younger versions of themselves. The show, created by Downton Abbey's Julian Fellowes, is being developed by NBC and could potentially debut as early as September if plans move forward.

Steven Gerrard is set to start for Liverpool in their FA Cup semi-final against Aston Villa at Wembley, marking what could be his final appearance at the national stadium before joining LA Galaxy. Manager Brendan Rodgers has selected Gerrard to lead the midfield, allowing him to potentially secure a trophy and a fitting end to his illustrious career in English football. Despite serving a recent three-match ban, Gerrard has shown readiness and special quality, contributing significantly to Liverpool's big-game performances.

A new Dr. Seuss book titled "What Pet Should I Get?" has generated significant interest, leading to an increased first printing from 500,000 to 1 million copies to meet demand. This marks the first new original Dr. Seuss book since 1990 and features characters from his classic "One Fish Two Fish Red Fish Blue Fish." The book, which was discovered in 2013 among the late Theodore Geisel's (Dr. Seuss) belongings, is set to debut on July 28, 2023.

Jessica Carey traveled over three hours to surprise her grandmother, Patty Lawing, with a tattoo of her younger self on Jessica's arm. The heartfelt gesture, captured on video by a relative, moved Patty to tears and elicited an emotional reaction. Jessica, along with her husband and two children, planned the surprise visit and tattoo to bring joy to Patty, who was unaware of the special gift until Jessica's arrival.

Annegret Raunigk, a 65-year-old German primary school teacher, is expecting quadruplets, making her the oldest known woman to carry such a pregnancy. She conceived through 18 months of fertility treatment, using donated sperm and eggs, and is currently in her 21st week of pregnancy. Despite her advanced age, Ms. Raunigk remains optimistic about the birth and highlights the importance of personal decision-making over societal opinions.

Japan's space agency, JAXA, plans to send an unmanned rover to the moon by 2018, aiming to join the select group of nations that have explored the lunar surface. The mission, which involves using JAXA’s Epsilon rocket to deploy the SLIM probe, seeks to develop soft-landing technologies potentially applicable to future missions to the moon or even Mars. This endeavor represents Japan's effort to compete with other Asian nations like China and India in space exploration.

A dengue fever outbreak in Brazil has prompted Brazilian football clubs to take precautionary measures, as several top players have fallen ill, including Corinthians striker Paolo Guerrero. To combat the issue, players are using insect repellent during practice and clubs are checking their facilities for potential mosquito breeding grounds. The increase in dengue cases has raised concerns among players, who fear missing crucial matches due to the prolonged recovery period required for the disease, which can cause severe joint pain and headaches.

Manchester United striker James Wilson expressed his admiration for Wayne Rooney, Robin van Persie, and Radamel Falcao, stating that he would most like to adopt Rooney's skill in taking free-kicks, van Persie's movement, and Falcao's instinctive positioning. Wilson, who has made 16 appearances for Manchester United this season, highlighted Rooney's daily practice of free-kicks as particularly impressive. In addition to his growing experience with the first team, Wilson continues to look to these established strikers for guidance and inspiration.

Archie Brown Jr., a 39-year-old van driver from Milwaukee, Wisconsin, was fatally shot at the scene after striking and killing a 2-year-old child who ran in front of his vehicle. Shortly after, a 15-year-old boy was also shot and later died, though his connection to the incident remains unclear. Police suggest the shooting may have been in revenge for the child's death, but no suspects have been arrested yet.

A child from Memphis, Tennessee, with a baby face, has gained over 3,000 Twitter followers by posting pictures of himself in "gang life" situations, including with guns and drugs, which have drawn criticism from the public. Despite the backlash, the boy defended his actions, citing personal hardships and challenging his critics. Authorities are becoming more aware of how social media, including platforms like Twitter, can be used to promote gang culture.

Former Redgum frontman John Schumann criticized anti-Islam protesters for using his song "I Was Only 19" at Reclaim Australia rallies, which aimed to oppose sharia law and Islamization. Schumann stated that the song promotes compassion, tolerance, and inclusiveness, contradicting the rally's message. Violence erupted during the rallies, resulting in several arrests and minor injuries, prompting political leaders to condemn the violence and discourage the spread of misinformation about Islam in Australia.

Emmanuel Adebayor, a forward for Tottenham, has used Twitter to express his commitment to staying with the club despite rumors of potential moves away. The 31-year-old Togo international, who joined Tottenham in 2011, claims he will continue to fight for a place in the starting lineup at White Hart Lane. However, his recent form has been criticized, and he faces stiff competition from the rising star Harry Kane, leading some to question his future at the club.

Stuart Pearce advocates for Manchester City to retain Manuel Pellegrini, believing he should be given more time to improve the team's performance despite their recent struggles. The club's disappointment is evident, particularly after their loss to Manchester United, and Pearce emphasizes that the manager should not be replaced hastily. He also criticizes Yaya Toure's impact on the team, suggesting that his decline in form and absences have significantly affected the team's results, while acknowledging that Sergio Aguero remains a bright spot in an otherwise underperforming squad.

Steve Bruce remains optimistic about keeping Hull City in the Premier League despite a 2-0 loss to Southampton that leaves them struggling to avoid relegation. Bruce believes that securing nine or eight more wins could secure their place in the league, though they face tough upcoming matches against top teams like Liverpool, Arsenal, Tottenham, and Manchester United. Bruce attributes their current difficulties to extended injuries to key players, although he remains confident they can overcome these challenges.

A full-scale terror alert was triggered in Reading when a member of the public reported seeing a barge with a fake missile launcher and a dummy in a balaclava on the Thames. Thames Valley Police and an Army bomb disposal team responded, only to find that the "weapon" was a non-threatening, purely ornamental model. The prankster's actions caused unnecessary panic, prompting local residents to criticize the stunt as both stupid and inappropriate given the current security climate.

Tiger Woods suffered an unusual injury during his play at the Masters, hitting his club into a tree root on the ninth hole and causing significant pain in his right wrist. Despite the setback, Woods managed to continue playing and finished the tournament at 5-under-par, marking his best performance in over a year. His final position was tied for 17th, 13 strokes behind the tournament winner, 21-year-old Jordan Spieth.

Iker Casillas asserts his intention to remain at Real Madrid despite potential competition from David de Gea, stating he will fight for the starting goalkeeper position. Casillas, who has dedicated his entire career to the club since 1996, emphasizes his commitment to fulfilling his contract. He also expresses optimism about Real Madrid's chances to retain the Champions League title, viewing the upcoming semi-finals as a battle between four formidable European teams.

Embarrassing footage has surfaced of a failed missile launch in Russia, showing an S300 rocket barely lifting off before plummeting back to the ground, causing a small explosion and significant debris. This incident adds to the embarrassment for President Vladimir Putin, whose defense budget has increased by 33% over the past year. The video, which also includes a previous failed rocket launch that killed six Russian missile technicians, highlights issues within the Russian military despite budget growth.

Lancashire County Cricket Club has signed Australian all-rounder James Faulkner as their overseas player for the majority of the summer. Faulkner, who recently won the World Cup with Australia, will join the team after completing his Indian Premier League commitments and replacing his compatriot Peter Siddle. The club expresses excitement about Faulkner's addition, highlighting his world-class status and potential benefits for both first-class and limited-overs cricket.

Mary Kay Letourneau Fualaau, who served over seven years in prison for having an affair with a 13-year-old student, has remarried and celebrated her 10th wedding anniversary with her husband Vili Fualaau. The couple, now 53 and 31 respectively, will discuss their relationship and marriage on an upcoming "20/20" interview with Barbara Walters, where they will share insights into what keeps their relationship strong despite the significant age gap and past challenges.

Jamie Carragher traveled to Spain during the international break to watch his son James play in the Under 12s Mediterranean International Cup, a prestigious youth tournament featuring clubs from over 36 countries. During his trip, Carragher appeared on local television and shared photos from the event on his Instagram, cheering as Liverpool U12s drew 1-1 with a local Catalan team. The tournament, now in its 15th year, has hosted many renowned players including Philippe Coutinho, Lionel Messi, and Neymar in its history.

Seattle-based filmmaker Gabriel Ng spent three months in Thailand to create a breathtaking six-minute video showcasing the country's beauty spots and everyday life. Filmed primarily on the island of Ko Samui using a remote control drone, the video features stunning coastal scenes, religious sites, and moments of daily life. The footage has gained significant attention on YouTube, with viewers praising the quality and comparing it to professional productions.

Peter Moores expressed his willingness to work with Michael Vaughan if he becomes England's new director of cricket, emphasizing that it is not a personal issue but rather about improving the team. Moores believes additional voices in the dressing room might not be necessary, depending on the responsibilities assigned to the new role. Despite the recent restructuring of England's cricket management, Moores remains focused on his coaching duties and is optimistic about upcoming Test matches, while also expressing gratitude towards the departing Paul Downton.

Nottingham Forest intends to pursue a transfer for Blackburn's striker Jordan Rhodes, valued at £10 million, with Forest manager Dougie Freedman hoping a direct cash offer will succeed where previous attempts failed. Blackburn initially rejected Forest's earlier bid in March, but now faces renewed interest as Rhodes has demonstrated his value by scoring 70 goals in the past three seasons. Additionally, Blackburn's Gary Bowyer anticipates further interest in striker Rudy Gestede, who recently scored 19 goals, including one against Forest.

In a video captured in Bahama, North Carolina, a trio of dogs—Sky (a Husky), Sadie (a brown and white Springer Spaniel), and Marshall (a black and white Springer Spaniel)—produce a unique musical ensemble by howling and barking in harmony. Starting with Sadie initiating the sounds, the Husky Sky follows with a more melodious howl, and both dogs engage in a musical interaction, with Marshall adding excitement from the side. The performance reaches a climax as all three dogs howl together in perfect harmony before being interrupted by their owner.

Alain Robert, known as the 'French Spiderman,' scaled the 1,007-foot Cayan Tower in Dubai without a safety harness, using only sticky tape and chalk for assistance. This daring climb, which took him over an hour and a half, was witnessed by hundreds of spectators and captured on video. Robert, who has faced numerous falls and legal issues during previous climbs, has previously ascended the world's tallest building, the Burj Khalifa, though he adhered to safety regulations on that occasion.

An experimental cancer drug previously discontinued due to poor results showed promise in reversing Alzheimer's symptoms in mice, according to researchers at Yale University. The drug, AZD05030, works by blocking a process that damages nerve connections in the brain responsible for memory storage. Now in human trials, the initial success in mice has prompted further investigation into its potential benefits for Alzheimer's patients.

The article discusses recent reveals from Marvel Studios regarding their upcoming films and TV shows, including the appearance of the Vision in "Avengers: Age of Ultron," the release of the real red suit for Charlie Cox's Daredevil in the new Netflix series, and the casting of Ben Hardy as the character Angel for "X-Men: Apocalypse." It also mentions the unveiling of Jamie Bell's character, The Thing, in the rebooted "Fantastic Four" movie, and the continued popularity of superhero content across various media platforms.

Veteran referee Kenny Bayless will officiate the highly anticipated fight between Floyd Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao, having previously worked with both fighters in numerous matches. Despite his reputation as one of the best referees in the world, some, like former opponent Oscar De La Hoya, believe Bayless's involvement gives Mayweather an unfair advantage due to Bayless breaking up clinches more frequently in Mayweather's favor. The appointment has sparked debate among boxing enthusiasts regarding its potential impact on the outcome of the historic fight.

Harry Kane's participation in the upcoming Under 21 European Championship is uncertain due to Tottenham Hotspur's scheduled post-season friendly in Malaysia. The club's manager, Mauricio Pochettino, is concerned about the potential for burnout, while the Football Association is in discussions with Tottenham about Kane's availability. Kane himself wishes to play for the Under 21 side, but the club is prioritizing his rest for the upcoming season.

A measles outbreak affecting over 130 people in California, primarily linked to visits to Disney theme parks, has concluded according to the California Department of Public Health. During the outbreak, 70% of those whose vaccination status could be confirmed were found to be unvaccinated, highlighting the role of vaccination in preventing such outbreaks. The successful containment of the outbreak was attributed to prompt case investigations, vaccination of at-risk individuals, and increased awareness among healthcare providers.

In Argentina, police are searching for a family of six who were photographed riding on a single motorbike without helmets, with two adults and four children aboard, in the city of San Miguel de Tucuman. This incident follows a similar case in Junín where a family of seven was captured on camera using the same method. Both families faced widespread condemnation on social media for their perceived irresponsibility and dangerous behavior.

A 44-year-old woman named Andrea McVeigh was seriously injured after being hit by a cyclist while walking on the pavement in Bermondsey, south London. The cyclist fled the scene, prompting a police investigation and the release of CCTV footage. McVeigh suffered significant facial injuries and is now scarred for life, while also facing ongoing physical and emotional recovery.

The headstone of Hillary Clinton’s father, Hugh Rodham, was found tipped over in a cemetery in Scranton, Pennsylvania, just days after Clinton announced her presidential campaign. While police suspect vandalism, no other nearby headstones were damaged, and some believe the timing is coincidental rather than conspiratorial. Funeral director Neil Regan and local resident Paul McGloin, who regularly tends to the gravesite, do not rule out weather-related causes but consider vandalism the most likely explanation.

A California woman, Beatriz Paez, was recording police activity when a U.S. marshal allegedly took her phone, broke it with his foot, and kicked it away, according to a video recorded by another witness. Paez, who felt her safety was compromised during the incident, has filed a complaint with local police and is considering legal action. The U.S. Marshals Service is currently reviewing the incident, while a federal investigation may be warranted given the circumstances, as per a request made by a local representative.

Max, a 18.5-inch-tall corgi-Siberian husky cross, has been abandoned and is now at the Dogs Trust in Basildon, Essex, where he has become a favorite among the staff. Max's small stature, despite being fully grown, and his gentle, intelligent nature make him an appealing pet, though the charity notes that many similar wolf-like breeds end up abandoned due to unprepared new owners struggling to meet their specific needs.

Chilean pickpockets have emerged as the most effective thieves operating in central London, targeting wealthy tourists in areas such as the West End. According to undercover police, these gangs, often operating in groups of three to six, use intelligence to target high-value items from tourists and employ tactics like blending in as families or businessmen to avoid suspicion. The Metropolitan Police, while reporting a 50% reduction in thefts, continue to monitor these organized international gangs, which frequently move between cities in Europe to evade detection.

In a severe car accident in Southam, Warwickshire, a young driver survived a crash where his vehicle flipped and trapped him underneath. Despite suffering head, chest, and leg injuries, the man remained conscious throughout the rescue operation, which took 25 minutes with the help of firefighters using specialized equipment. Emergency services praised the quick response of a community paramedic who began treating the victim shortly after the incident.

Fly-tippers have dumped an astounding 40 tonnes of industrial waste along the roadside in the Suffolk village of Walsham-le-Willows, prompting concerns over the environmental impact and costing thousands of pounds to clean up. Described by a police officer as the worst case of flytipping he has seen in nearly 30 years, the waste includes materials from the carpet and veterinary industries and was allegedly transported using three tractors and trailers. Authorities, including the police, National Farmers' Union, and Country Land and Business Association, are working together to address the issue and prevent future incidents.

At Toronto's Pearson International Airport, a man who refused to comply with security staff was tasered and brought to the ground, attempting to enter a restricted area despite being told he could not board his flight. The incident was captured on video, showing the man mumbling and holding a black briefcase tightly as he was tasered, after which he stood visibly shaking before being subdued by police. The man was later transferred to a nearby hospital under the Mental Health Act, with no indication of criminal charges being pursued.

Serbia's President Tomislav Nikolic's government jet had to return to Belgrade after the co-pilot accidentally spilled coffee on the instrument panel, causing the plane to lose altitude and resulting in a turbulent descent. The co-pilot, Bojan Zoric, mistakenly activated the emergency slat button while wiping the coffee spill, which deactivated the autopilot system. Following the incident, Zoric's license was suspended, and an investigation found that one of the engines also stopped working briefly during the return flight.

In South Africa, over 300 suspects have been arrested in connection with violent attacks targeting foreigners, which have forced thousands to seek refuge in temporary shelters. These attacks, which occurred primarily in Durban, have resulted in multiple casualties and have been condemned by the government, which has praised law enforcement for preventing further violence. Despite the xenophobic sentiment, there has been an outpouring of support from South Africans who are appalled by the attacks and reminding the nation of its shared history of reliance on African neighbors during challenging times.

A skier named Zach Birnie captured harrowing footage of himself becoming entangled in an avalanche while skiing off-piste in Revelstoke, Canada. Despite the terrifying experience, Birnie managed to escape with only a slight shoulder injury, though he was buried under the snow for a significant period. Experts attribute the avalanche to the combination of fresh snow and steep terrain, and advise those caught in similar situations to try to escape the avalanche area, release their ski poles, and protect their faces.

On the hottest day of the year, two bare-chested men in their 20s attempted to rob an Esso petrol station in Caterham, Surrey, forcing their way into the manager's office to search for cash but were interrupted by staff and fled without taking any money. Police have released CCTV footage of the suspects and are appealing for public assistance in identifying them. A third suspect has been arrested and released on bail.

The Lada Niva 4x4, starting at £13,395 on the road, is gaining popularity despite its Soviet-era roots, particularly due to its robust design and affordable price compared to luxury alternatives like the Land Rover Defender. While it lacks modern amenities, this simplicity means the interior can be easily cleaned after off-road adventures. Interestingly, even Russian President Vladimir Putin used a Niva, though he reportedly replaced its Russian engine with a German one.

A lawsuit has been filed against the nation's largest supplier of HIV and AIDS medical care, the AIDS Healthcare Foundation, accusing the company of a $20 million scam over 12 states involving kickbacks for patient referrals to boost funding from federal health programs. Former managers claim the company paid employees and patients $100 bonuses for referring positive test results and implemented this scheme starting in 2010. Despite these allegations, the foundation's president maintains they have not done anything wrong and argues that the government's decision not to intervene speaks to the merit of their case.

Liz, a bearded dragon owned by Shannen Hussein, appears to understand and respond to human speech, nodding her head when asked if she's hungry and then enjoying a superworm treat as a reward. Liz shares the spotlight with other pets on Shannen's social media channels, including the viral sensation Winter, a pet lamb known for her playful antics. Shannen runs a hobby farm where various animals like cats, birds, a snake, and even a llama and an emu live and feature in her online content.

A West Virginia man named Travis Hatfield gained viral attention for posting a video of him singing a George Jones song to his uncle, Jamie Joe Cline, who has Down syndrome. The heartfelt performance, which has been viewed over 410,000 times, showcases their weekly musical duets and has inspired Travis to pursue a career in country music. Travis dreams of a record deal and plans to audition for The Voice and release an album with 12 original songs.

Nik Wallenda, a high-wire performer and member of the 'Flying Wallenda' family, announced that he will attempt to walk untethered on top of the 400-foot Orlando Eye observation wheel in Orlando, Florida, on April 29. The Orlando Eye, which will open to the public on May 4, offers views from 30 enclosed capsules. This stunt, which sets itself apart from previous challenges due to the larger scale of the wheel and the absence of a safety pole, marks another daring feat for Wallenda, who has previously walked across the Grand Canyon and Niagara Falls.

Medhi Benatia, a central defender for Bayern Munich, is likely to miss both legs of the Champions League quarter-final against Porto due to a muscle injury sustained during a German Cup match. The injury, which could keep him out for two to four weeks, adds to Bayern's already lengthy injury list. Despite the setback, Bayern Munich remains a strong contender for multiple titles, including the Bundesliga championship, with some players returning to training.

Bayern Munich secured a dominant 6-1 victory over Porto in the Champions League quarter-final second leg, advancing to the semi-finals and continuing their impressive form under Pep Guardiola. This performance brought their season total to 115 goals, with the team showing no signs of slowing down, as they still have five Bundesliga matches, a German Cup semi-final, and potential Champions League games to go. At their current pace, Bayern could end the season with an astonishing 141 goals, putting immense pressure on other European teams to match their scoring prowess.

Fernando Torres credits Diego Simeone as the key figure behind Atletico Madrid's recent success and their upcoming Champions League match against Real Madrid. Since Simeone's leadership, Atletico Madrid has become one of Europe's top teams, having not lost to Real Madrid in six consecutive matches. Torres emphasizes that Simeone's understanding of the team's strengths and weaknesses is crucial to their performance.

A light aircraft crash occurred near Loch Etive in western Scotland, resulting in the discovery of two bodies among the wreckage. Search and rescue operations involving lifeboats, helicopters, and police were initiated after the plane lost contact with ground control while en route from central Scotland to Tiree. Police Scotland is investigating the circumstances of the crash and urging anyone with information to come forward.

A bus shattered the windscreen of a Boeing 777 passenger jet at Tashkent airport in Uzbekistan, causing significant damage and potentially delaying numerous passengers due to the airport's high traffic volume. This incident, among others involving aircraft collisions at major airports, highlights the increasing frequency of such accidents despite safety measures. Recent examples include Ryanair planes colliding at Dublin Airport and a British Airways plane hitting a hangar at Heathrow, emphasizing the need for improved safety protocols in airport operations.

An off-duty Secret Service agent, Arthur Baldwin, was arrested in Washington D.C. for attempting to break into a house and causing property damage, leading to the revocation of his security clearance and placement on leave. His arrest comes shortly after another high-ranking supervisor was placed on leave amid accusations of misconduct, highlighting ongoing issues within the agency. These incidents have tarnished the Secret Service's reputation, following previous controversies including an incident where officials allegedly entered a restricted area of the White House while intoxicated.

Israel is developing a unique tunnelling detection system, designed to accurately identify tunneling activities from a distance without false alarms. This advanced system, a collaboration between Elbit Systems and the Israeli Ministry of Defense, aims to enhance security along the Gaza-Israel border and comes after the consideration of over 700 proposals. While the project is expected to be costly—approximately £2.3 million per mile—the system has already passed initial tests and is anticipated to be installed within a year.

A primary school headteacher has implemented a water-only drink policy during school hours to promote long-term pupil health, but the decision has sparked a campaign by parents who argue it is too restrictive and goes against their choices for their children. While the headteacher defends the policy as beneficial for students' health, critics view it as overly stringent and a "joke." This ban follows similar measures taken in other schools, which have also faced parental opposition.

Paul Smith has secured a significant fight against undefeated Andre Ward on June 20 in Oakland, California. This opportunity comes after Smith's previous attempts to challenge for the WBO title were unsuccessful, and it represents a major step for Smith, who aims to prove himself against one of the sport's top pound-for-pound fighters. Despite Ward's long absence from the ring, Smith is confident and eager to take on the challenge, stating that he cannot wait to test himself against such a talented opponent.

German Chancellor Angela Merkel spent Easter on the island of Ischia in Italy, where she and her husband, chemist Joachim Sauer, typically stay at the luxurious five-star Miramare Spa Hotel. Despite the cool weather and lack of sunshine, Mrs. Merkel focused on healthy activities like Pilates and vegetarian meals rather than sunbathing or using the hotel's pools. Merkel's husband, known for avoiding the public eye, was present but largely kept to the background, as he often does during their annual holiday.

Ander Herrera, a Manchester United midfielder, has scored several goals without looking at the ball or the goal, including a brace against Aston Villa where his eyes appeared to be shut during both shots. This unusual goal-scoring technique has been observed in multiple matches, though Herrera did score one goal with his eyes open against Yeovil in January. Manchester United manager Louis van Gaal noted that Herrera needs to improve his ball control before shooting.

A 23-month-old toddler tragically died after being struck by her father's pickup truck in the driveway of their North Las Vegas home. The father and other family members were unaware that the toddler had ventured outside. The incident was ruled an accident, and no charges were filed.

The University of Connecticut baseball team has welcomed 5-year-old Grayson Hand, a child battling leukemia, as its newest member with the help of Team IMPACT. Grayson will join the team, have his own locker, and attend games and practices, while his sister Sophie has been named an honorary cheerleader. This partnership, according to Grayson's father, symbolizes the emotional support the family has received from the community.

A passenger on a London Midland train discovered excrement in a newspaper on the floor, causing significant delays and the cancellation of a service between Lichfield Trent Valley and Longbridge. London Midland has vowed to provide police with CCTV footage of the alleged perpetrator, while the train had to be cleaned before services could resume. This incident follows a similar case where a British Airways flight was forced to return to London due to a foul odor from a toilet overflow.

James Rodriguez, who moved to Real Madrid for £60 million from Monaco last summer, has proven to be a valuable asset to the team, with Real Madrid winning 80% of their matches when he is in the lineup, according to Spanish newspaper Marca. Rodriguez is referred to as "the jewel in Real Madrid's crown" and has become a fan favorite despite his high price tag. Meanwhile, in Italy, La Gazzetta dello Sport reports that former Manchester City manager Roberto Mancini plans to make significant changes to Inter Milan by signing eight new players this summer.

A Florida man named Kenneth Crowder, believed to be under the influence of the powerful drug Flakka, attacked a police officer after being tased twice, claiming he was God and attempting to stab the officer with a police badge. Crowder was arrested and charged with battery on a law-enforcement officer, resisting with violence, and assault with a deadly weapon on a law-enforcement officer. Flakka, a potent synthetic drug similar to cathinone, has been linked to increased incidents of violent behavior and psychosis among its users.

During a Russian Premier League match between Arsenal Tula and Torpedo Moscow, a brawl among fans led to the game being suspended for seven minutes as Torpedo supporters broke barriers and threw seats at law enforcement. The referee halted the match, and despite order eventually being restored, Torpedo won 3-1. The club faces severe punishment due to this incident, which marks another instance of fan violence for Torpedo, who have been sanctioned multiple times this season for similar behavior.

High school girls in Huizhou, China, are undergoing military-style dagger drills as part of their self-defense training under the guidance of former special forces soldier Inspector Tan. Although the knives used in the training are fake and pose no danger, the girls are learning techniques that could be life-saving, using any sharp object available to them, including everyday items like chopsticks and forks. The training, which involves a series of eight movements and takes five days, is widely popular among the participants, who also practice shouting commands like "kill, stab, slash, and jab" during the sessions.

AP McCoy, the champion jockey with a record of winning the title every year since 1997, is urging the nation to support his final chance at winning the Grand National with his mount Shutthefrontdoor, which would be a fairytale ending to his career. Despite the high expectations and the potential for a record-breaking win, McCoy acknowledges the unpredictability of the race and the sport of jump racing. He has vowed to retire immediately if they secure the victory, which would be a second win in the prestigious event.

John Isner advanced to the Miami Open semifinals with a straight-sets victory over Kei Nishikori, becoming the first American male to reach this stage since 2011. Isner showcased his powerful serve, not facing any break points in the match or during the tournament thus far. Meanwhile, Andy Murray will face Tomas Berdych in the other semifinal, with an interesting dynamic given their past rivalry and the recent coaching changes for Berdych.

Franz Beckenbauer, the German football legend, criticized Bayern Munich's performance in their Champions League quarter-final loss to Porto, likening it to players taking "sleeping pills." He specifically targeted defender Dante, jokingly comparing his performance to wearing "ski boots." Despite the harsh words, Beckenbauer maintained that Bayern still had a chance to progress, emphasizing the need for significant improvement if they were to advance to the semi-finals.

A 21-year-old man named Arnold Quintero from San Antonio, Texas, has been arrested for allegedly imprisoning, beating, sexually assaulting, and burning a 13-year-old girl with a lighter. Quintero faces multiple charges including aggravated sexual assault of a child, sex performed by a child under 14, and possession with intent to deliver, among others. The victim identified him through a photographic lineup about a month after reporting the abuse.

In Week 12 of the Betway Premier League, Michael van Gerwen and Gary Anderson each won and lost a game, showcasing an eventful night in darts. Van Gerwen secured a dominant 7-0 victory over James Wade and advanced to the May play-offs at the 02, but later lost to Gary Anderson. Anderson, after an initial loss to Stephen Bunting, won a thrilling match against Van Gerwen with an impressive average of 105.94.

Jay Rutland, the husband of billionaire heiress Tamara Ecclestone, earns just £65 a week from his company, which brought in £3,378 in the last financial year. Despite his low income, the couple, who live in a £45 million house, celebrate their lifestyle with expensive events like a £70,000 farmyard-themed birthday party for their daughter Sophia. The company's financial troubles and Jay Rutland's past issues, including a ban from trading and a mugging, highlight the stark contrast between the couple's modest business operations and their lavish personal spending.

A Chinese man named Jia Binhui, diagnosed with leukemia and unable to afford traditional medical treatment, has resorted to a homemade alternative therapy involving lying over hot coals in his backyard, believing that temperatures above 42 degrees Celsius can kill cancer cells. Despite the unconventional and dangerous nature of his self-imposed treatment, Jia has persisted, even marrying his long-term girlfriend while refusing to surrender to his illness. He plans to continue this method before seeking further conventional medical advice.

Leroy Fer, a Dutch midfielder for Queens Park Rangers, is expected to return to the squad ahead of their match against West Ham due to recover from a knee injury. Manager Chris Ramsey hopes to include Fer, though he acknowledges the player is not yet at full fitness. QPR is aiming to use this opportunity to bolster their chances against relegation, with several other players also returning to fitness.

In the final kilometre of the Scheldeprijs race, Team Sky's Elia Viviani was involved in a major crash that resulted in him being taken to the hospital for x-rays, while Team mates Sir Bradley Wiggins and Geraint Thomas managed to avoid the accident. Despite the crash, Team Sky still had a strong performance, with Alexander Kristoff from Katusha winning the race after only 14 riders contested the sprint finish.

Before their FA Cup semi-final against Liverpool, Aston Villa's players received supportive messages in their dressing room at Wembley Stadium. Young player Jack Grealish tweeted about a motivational message from fan Mike Shenaniganz Cope, encouraging the team to persevere through challenges and "find the end of the rainbow." Both Grealish and goalkeeper Brad Guzan shared their messages of support on social media, with Guzan's instructing the team to "fight like Lions."

A 12-year-old boy named Hanghang in central China suffered severe injuries when his old mobile phone exploded while charging, exposing parts of his jawbone and embedding fragments in his arms and legs. The explosion occurred after Hanghang used the phone as an alarm and noticed it was hot before it blew up in his face. Doctors at Ping Mei Group Hospital expect multiple surgeries to repair the extensive damage, and experts warn that improper charging is a common cause of such incidents.

Mike Rowe, known for his work on "Dirty Jobs," highlights the impactful work of Chad Pregracke, founder of Living Lands & Waters, a nonprofit dedicated to cleaning U.S. waterways. Since its inception in 1998, Pregracke and his volunteers have collected over 8.4 million pounds of trash from rivers across the country, earning him the 2013 CNN Hero of the Year Award. In an episode of "Somebody's Gotta Do It," Rowe tours Pregracke’s solar-powered barge and learns about their ongoing mission to remove an additional 500,000 pounds of trash in 2015.

The ancient Tuscan town of Balestrino, dating back to the 11th century, was captured in a drone video showcasing its eerie beauty and mysterious history. Once home to 800 inhabitants and owned by the Benedictine abbey of San Pietro dei Monti in the 1100s, the town was largely abandoned due to seismic instability, with an 1887 earthquake measuring 6.7 on the Richter scale causing significant damage. Today, considered one of Italy's most famous abandoned locations, the town is shrouded in folklore and rumored to be haunted, with some structures still standing while others are in various states of decay.

At an emotional event in Anaheim, California, the cast of "Star Wars: Episode VII — The Force Awakens" premiered a trailer for the upcoming film and introduced the BB8 droid, among other elements, to the enthusiastic audience. The event highlighted key moments such as Han Solo's return and the reveal of the new shooting location, Jakku, rather than Tatooine. Additionally, the director emphasized that the film would feature less CGI compared to the prequels, with much of the footage shot on actual sets.

Toronto's former Mayor Rob Ford announced he would undergo surgery to remove a cancerous tumor in his abdomen, having previously undergone chemotherapy and radiation treatment. Ford, who had been re-elected to his council seat, had been battling malignant liposarcoma, a rare form of soft tissue cancer, since being diagnosed last year. Despite his health struggles, Ford expressed optimism about his prognosis and hoped to return to work in September.

At the University of Cape Town, a long-standing campaign to remove the statue of Cecil Rhodes culminated in its removal, as the university received permission from the heritage authority. This action was seen by many students as a step towards a more Afrocentric educational environment, reflecting a desire to move away from symbols of colonialism and racism. However, the decision sparked controversy among Afrikaner groups who viewed the removal as an attempt to erase history, sparking debates about how to honor and learn from South Africa's complex past.

Michael Phelps, the 18-time Olympic gold medalist, returned to competitive swimming with a victory in the 100 meters butterfly at the Arena Pro Swim Series in Arizona, marking his first race since his six-month suspension due to a drink-driving conviction. Despite missing the upcoming World Championships, Phelps expressed his enjoyment of racing and confirmed his intention to compete in the 2016 Olympics in Rio de Janeiro.

A woman was found hanging from a fire escape in Crown Heights, New York, with her body left dangling for over an hour, according to reports. Neighbors expressed shock and trauma, with one thinking the scene was a Halloween prank. The woman, who had known neighbors described as "social" and "nice," had a history of mental health issues.

Lyon reclaimed the top spot in Ligue 1 after securing a 2-2 draw against Saint-Etienne in a thrilling Rhone Valley derby, thanks to goals from Clinton N'Jie and Christophe Jallet. Meanwhile, Lille maintained their pursuit of a top-four finish by defeating Bordeaux 2-0, with goals from Nolan Roux and Adama Traore. Additionally, Montpellier secured a narrow 1-0 victory over Caen through an early header by Brazilian defender Hilton, helping them move up to seventh place while leaving Caen in 13th.

Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger admits he did not anticipate that players like Hector Bellerin and Francis Coquelin would become such crucial figures in the team's late surge for the Premier League title. Bellerin, who previously had limited playing time at Watford, scored a critical goal against Liverpool and showcased his defensive skills against Raheem Sterling. Meanwhile, Coquelin, whom Wenger had nearly abandoned, has proven to be a valuable asset to the team.

Fox is developing a two-hour remake of the 1975 cult classic "The Rocky Horror Picture Show" for television, with plans to celebrate the film's 40th anniversary. Directed and executive-produced by Kenneth Ortega, the special will feature a cast yet to be determined and is expected to premiere sometime in the future. This project follows previous unsuccessful attempts to adapt the film into a television special and builds on earlier television ventures, such as "Glee's" musical tribute to the show.

Roma FC has been ordered to close part of their stadium for their next home game due to offensive banners displayed by fans during a match against Napoli. These banners insulted the mother of a Napoli fan who died in violent clashes following a previous match. As a result, the Stadio Olimpico will be partially closed for the upcoming league match against Atalanta on April 19th.

Ellen White scored a spectacular goal for Notts County against her former club, Arsenal, by taking a free kick and firing it into the corner of the net. This moment was particularly memorable for White, as it combined scoring against her old team with the successful execution of a well-practiced set-piece from training. Despite this highlight, White also missed a penalty opportunity and the game ended in a draw after Arsenal equalized late in the match.

Arsene Wenger maintains he has no regrets about not signing Eden Hazard in 2012, despite the Chelsea forward becoming one of the Premier League's standout players and winning the transfer of the year for joining Chelsea for £32 million. Wenger attributes the missed opportunity to financial constraints and the high costs involved at the time. Despite the regrettable decision, Wenger believes both Hazard and his current player Alexis Sanchez are in contention for the Player of the Year award, praising Hazard's improved performance and maturity over the past season.

Stephen Akers-Belcher, the Mayor of Hartlepool, was dismissed from his care manager role at Newcastle City Council after claiming to take paid leave for a funeral but being found at HMS Warrior, 323 miles away. The council denied claims that he was fired for whistleblowing, stating that an investigation into his allegations found no further action was necessary. Akers-Belcher maintained his innocence, but the council insisted he was dismissed for gross misconduct due to his failure to provide evidence supporting his claimed attendance at a funeral.

Dr. John Parker, a humanitarian doctor who had been working in an Ebola treatment clinic in Sierra Leone, was taken to Westmead Hospital in Sydney with flu-like symptoms but tested negative for the Ebola virus. Dr. Parker had recently returned to Australia after working in West Africa and had followed protocol by notifying authorities. NSW Health confirmed that no further testing for Ebola was required.

A schoolboy named Frankie Franz, inspired by Barcelona's Martin Montoya, successfully replicated a 27-yard goal into a basketball hoop, much to the amazement of his mother. The nine-year-old, who plays for Dagenham and Redbridge Football Club, managed to score the trick shot on his first attempt after moving the basketball hoop to the center of the goal. Frankie's mother expressed disbelief at her son's achievement, noting that he had succeeded not once, but twice, and seemed equally surprised by his own feat.

The Wisden–MCC Cricket Photograph of the Year 2014 short-list features captivating images of cricket players ranging from amateur enthusiasts to professional stars, capturing moments from around the world. Notably, Matthew Lewis won the competition with an image of West Indies player Dwayne Bravo making an extraordinary catch during the ICC World Twenty20. The collection also includes heartwarming and dramatic scenes such as children playing cricket on a Bangladesh rubbish tip and the 'world's highest game of cricket' played on Mount Kilimanjaro.

In a custody dispute, a New Jersey judge ruled that a mother's decision to take her 11-year-old daughter to a Pink concert was not evidence of bad parenting, despite the father's objections. The judge found the performances to be appropriate for a preteen and noted that the mother had made an informed decision after reviewing the content. The judge emphasized that the mother did not exceed reasonable parental judgment and that the concert did not pose any risks to the child.

Salcombe, a coastal town in Devon, has overtaken London in average property prices, with the average cost of a property in Salcombe reaching £671,759, compared to £638,217 in London. The waterfront properties in Salcombe are particularly expensive, with an average value topping £2 million, surpassing some of London's priciest areas such as Notting Hill and Regent's Park. As a result, Salcombe has become a sought-after destination for both buyers and holidaymakers looking to enjoy its luxurious seaside lifestyle.

Celtic have expressed dissatisfaction with the ticket prices set by the Scottish FA for their upcoming Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness Caledonian Thistle at Hampden Park. Celtic argue that the North Stand tickets are too expensive for many supporters and suggest that the pricing should be more equitable. The Scottish FA has defended its decision, stating that all participating clubs were consulted, and that the ticket prices have remained the same for the past four years.

Rebecca Rice, a 16-year-old student struggling with exam nerves, was allowed to bring her pet Labrador, Holly, into her GCSE French oral exam at Bodmin College in Cornwall. This unconventional support helped Rebecca remain calm during the five-minute test. The school, which has implemented various stress-reduction strategies, such as allowing drinks and friends in the room, found this approach particularly effective for Rebecca.

Anders Lindegaard, the goalkeeper for Manchester United, recently shared a photo of himself and his wife Misse Beqiri enjoying the English sun, reminding fans of their marriage during a day off. Lindegaard, who has had limited playing time with the team, has been linked to potential transfers but remains third-choice behind David de Gea and Victor Valdes. Off the pitch, however, the couple, who have been together since 2012 and got married in Mauritius, appear to be thriving, with Beqiri known for her modeling work and attractive presence on social media.

Spanish goalkeepers David de Gea and Victor Valdes took a much-needed break from the pressures of the season by visiting a theme park in England. Their recent performance has been impressive, with Manchester United securing six consecutive Premier League wins, including a notable victory over Manchester City, which has put them in contention for a top-four finish. However, uncertainty looms over their futures with both players' positions at the club being questioned due to Valdes' limited first-team opportunities since joining on a free transfer.

A 75-year-old piano teacher named John Goodwin, who was awaiting trial for charges of sexually assaulting an underage student, shot himself outside a New Hampshire courthouse while the jury was deliberating. Goodwin, who had faced six counts of aggravated felonious sexual assault, had claimed he was merely "touchy-feely" with his former student, now 24, and that the student did not come forward earlier due to embarrassment. The former student only reported the alleged assaults in 2013.

Amazon removed the controversial game "Rescue the Anorexia Girl" after it faced numerous complaints, as the game encouraged players to feed a cartoon character battling anorexia by throwing food at her. The game, marketed by SmartTouch Media, allowed players to become a "hero" by saving the anorexic girl from starvation, but it was widely criticized for potentially stigmatizing those with eating disorders and reinforcing harmful stereotypes. Critics argued that such a game trivializes a serious mental health issue and could discourage individuals from seeking help.

Scientists are attempting to create an artificial brain modeled after the honeybee's, aiming to develop drones that think, sense, and act like these insects. This project, known as the Green Brain Project, involves collaboration between researchers from the Universities of Sheffield and Sussex. So far, they have successfully cloned the visual processing part of the bee's brain, allowing a drone to fly in a manner similar to a honeybee.

A newly-wed couple from Air Malta celebrated their marriage by taking a romantic flight over the Mediterranean in a passenger jet that flew in the shape of two giant hearts shortly after takeoff. The unusual flight path, which included two circuits around Malta and a section skirting the Italian coast, was arranged to celebrate the marriage of a pilot and a cabin crew member, with the couple and their guests enjoying a short sight-seeing tour. The flight was noted on the airport's arrival board with the message 'Just Married,' and while some saw it as a creative training flight, others speculated it could have been a PR stunt or even a marriage proposal.

At a Norwegian zoo on Easter Monday, a five-year-old giraffe named Melvin died after being gored by an eland antelope in an unprovoked attack. The tragic incident occurred when Melvin got his head stuck in the enclosure's fence, causing the eland to react aggressively. Shocked witnesses, including around 30 people and several children, reported that the event was extremely traumatic, with some visitors even crying.

A Belgian mother, Gitte Denteneer, was shocked and outraged to find a charge of 50 cents for heating up her baby's feeding bottle on her restaurant bill at the Rubens cafe in Leuven. Her tweet about the incident went viral, sparking widespread criticism of the restaurant manager's "stingy" practice. The Horeca Vlaanderen restaurant chain, which owns the Rubens Cafe, clarified that such charges are rare and typically only applied if specifically mentioned to customers.

North Korea has accused Mexico of illegally detaining one of its cargo ships, the Mu Du Bong, which ran aground off Mexico's coast in July. Mexico defended its action, citing that the ship's owner, North Korea's Ocean Maritime Management company, had circumvented United Nations sanctions. Meanwhile, North Korea claims the ship is peaceful and demands its release and the return of its crew.

Prime Minister David Cameron plans to introduce an additional 600,000 free childcare places for children aged three to four, promising to provide up to 30 hours of free childcare weekly, which is expected to benefit over 9 million children annually. This initiative aims to address the high cost of childcare as a barrier to employment, particularly for second earners, and is funded by reducing tax relief on pension contributions for those earning over £150,000. Cameron emphasizes that this measure aligns with the Conservative Party's values of rewarding hard work and reducing poverty through employment.

Manchester City secured their place in the Youth Cup final by scoring two late goals against Leicester City, extending their first-leg lead to 5-1 on aggregate. The goals came from substitutes Isaac Buckley and Brandon Barker, despite Layton Ndukwu giving Leicester hope with a penalty. This sets up a final against Chelsea for Manchester City, who will play the first leg at their academy stadium on April 20 and the second at Stamford Bridge on April 27.

During a nationally broadcast Q&A session, Russian President Vladimir Putin dismissed Western sanctions imposed after the annexation of Crimea and the conflict in eastern Ukraine, predicting they would not end soon. He defended Russia's decision to lift a ban on selling advanced air defense systems to Iran, asserting that such a system served as a defensive measure and was not a threat to Israel.
